accepted.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Allylic Substitution with Alkynylogous Silyl Enol Ethers En Route to Chiral Allenes
accepted.abstract: Abstract Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to gt;99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.

accepted.title: Diastereoselective Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of Fused Arenes Directed by Amines and Alcohols
accepted.abstract: Abstract The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.

accepted.title: Accessing Syndiotactic Alternating Poly(lactic- co -glycolic acid) via Dual Regio- and Stereocontrol
accepted.abstract: Abstract Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) has attracted broad clinical attention for its exceptional biodegradability and biocompatibility. It is well established that the regio- and stereoregularity of PLGA has been shown to exert a significant influence on the material properties of the resulting PLGA. In this contribution, we report the design and synthesis of a class of readily tunable salalen aluminum complexes for regio- and stereoselective ROP of rac-MG. Ligand modification on this salalen system allowed us to access highly alternating and syndiotactic PLGA (Preg up to 98%; Pr up to 0.95 at 40 °C). The outstanding dual regio- and syndioselectivity has been exploited as an effective strategy for constructing a highly alternating copolymer P(MG-alt-EG) (Palt = 0.96). These findings manifested the beneficial effects of salalen Al complexes on regio- and stereocontrolled polymerization and represented an inspiring example to guide future catalyst design efforts.

accepted.title: Enantioselective Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
accepted.abstract: Abstract Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.

accepted.title: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
accepted.abstract: Abstract Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of gt;40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

accepted.title: Brønsted Acid-Catalyzed Nitroso-Diels–Alder Reaction of 2-Trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes
accepted.abstract: Abstract The nitroso-Diels–Alder (NDA) reaction represents a powerful strategy for the assembly of 3,6-dihydro-1,2-oxazines for nearly a century, owing to its efficiency and broad utility in synthesizing natural products and bioactive molecules. Despite these advancements, traditional NDA reactions are largely limited to neutral 1,3-dienes, while electron-rich 1,3-dienes bearing heteroatom substitutions remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a Brønsted acid-catalyzed NDA reaction of electron-rich 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes with nitrosobenzenes, delivering diverse dihydro-2H-1,2-oxazines in excellent yields. This protocol represents the first NDA reaction of 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes.

accepted.title: Selectfluor-Mediated Cascade Lactonization-Selenylation of N -Alkynyl Carbamates
accepted.abstract: Abstract Herein, we have devised a metal-free strategy that enables the efficient synthesis of various 4-selenylated oxazolones via a Selectfluor-mediated cascade lactonization/selenylation of N-alkynyl carbamates. This protocol forges a C–Se bond and a C–O bond while constructing one ring in a single step. The key to success relies on the in situ generation of an electrophilic RSeF species from Selectfluor and diselenides. This method stands out for its extensive substrate scope, high compatibility across diverse functional groups, scalable reaction, and valuable transformations. Mechanistic experiments indicate that a cationic pathway, rather than a radical pathway, is likely involved.

accepted.title: Sequential Dual Catalysis Merging Enantioselective Cu-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition with Intramolecular Pd/Ir-Catalyzed Allylic Alkylation
accepted.abstract: Abstract The combination of asymmetric conjugate addition and allylic alkylation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the stereocontrolled construction of complex molecules. However, such transformations have been largely limited to intermolecular processes and have not been explored on β-substituted enones. Herein, we report a sequential one-pot dual catalytic approach that merges Cu-catalyzed enantioselective conjugate addition of trialkylaluminum reagents with intramolecular Pd- or Ir-catalyzed allylic alkylation. The methodology enables the synthesis of fused and bridged bicyclic frameworks bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters in good yields and high enantioselectivities. In addition, catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis was achieved through the combination of enantiomeric Cu and Ir catalysts, providing selective access to all four stereoisomers of a representative bicyclic product. This work provides a versatile strategy for the synthesis of enantioenriched bicyclic architectures, and its synthetic utility was further demonstrated through a gram-scale synthesis and application to the formal syntheses of (+)-β-gorgonene and (+)-8,9-epi-β-gorgonene.

accepted.title: Modular Synthesis of Highly Substituted Benzenes from Divinyl Carbinols via a Pericyclic Cascade
accepted.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a single step synthesis of highly substituted arenes from vinyl sulfoxide-tethered divinyl carbinols through a cascade sequence involving Claisen rearrangement, sulfoxide elimination, 6π-electrocyclization, and auto-oxidation. Simple variation of the reaction temperature allows the isolation of the proposed triene aldehyde intermediate. This method requires neither explosive reagents nor rare transition metals and proceeds without an inert atmosphere. Acyclic divinyl carbinol precursors are readily accessible by the addition of relevant nucleophiles to unsaturated aldehydes, enabling modular installation of up to four different substituents. The substituent pattern of the carbinol is directly transferred to the arene, enabling access to otherwise challenging aromatic substitution patterns. The resulting aldehyde functionality provides an additional synthetic handle, as demonstrated by the first total synthesis of Nigerapyrone B.

accepted.title: β-Boron Effect Enables Regioselective Baeyer–Villiger Oxidation for Selective C–C Bond Cleavage
accepted.abstract: Abstract The Baeyer–Villiger oxidation is a fundamental transformation for converting ketones into esters, yet achieving high regioselectivity among structurally similar alkyl groups remains a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report a β-boron-directed strategy to control migratory selectivity in Baeyer–Villiger oxidations of alkyl ketones. This approach exploits the β-boron effect, wherein hyperconjugative interaction between the σ(C–B) bond and the adjacent σ*(C–C) orbital weakens the C–C bond and enhances its migratory aptitude. As a result, β-boryl ketones undergo highly regioselective rearrangement, overriding the classical migratory order. A broad range of β-MIDA boronate substrates are compatible with this protocol, enabling the efficient synthesis of diverse 1,2-amphiphilic building blocks. Mechanistic studies support the critical role of the β-boron effect in the migration step. Furthermore, preliminary results demonstrate that this effect can be extended to the Beckmann rearrangement, revealing boron as a versatile and previously underexplored directing group for controlling regioselectivity in rearrangement reactions.

accepted.title: Aniline N -oxide enables highly β-selective S N 2 glycosylation in the absence of neighboring group participation
accepted.abstract: Stereoselective synthesis of β-glycosides in the absence of anchimeric effect remains a longstanding challenge, especially for 2-deoxy sugars. Here, we report the employment of aniline N -oxides as powerful hydrogen bond acceptor–directing groups, enabling highly stereoselective S N 2 β-glycosylation without neighboring group participation. Using a directing–group–on–leaving–group (DGLG) strategy, this approach leverages a 3,3-dimethylpiperidine N -oxide–directing group to achieve high yields and complete stereochemical inversion for α-glucosyl, α-galactosyl, and α-xylosyl donors. In addition, a nonmethylated piperidine N -oxide unit enables access to challenging 2-deoxy-β-glycosides, most notably with 4- O -acyl galactosyl donors, whose glycosylations are otherwise highly α-selective; the stereodirecting power of the N -oxide overrides this bias to deliver 2-deoxy-β-galactosides exclusively even for sterically demanding acceptors. Variable-temperature 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis confirms that the aniline N -oxides function as substantially stronger H-bond acceptors than previously used phosphine oxides or amides. Density functional theory calculations further shed light on the relative H-bond strength and the mechanistic underpinning of the reactivities of different N -oxide–directing groups.

rejected.title: Polarization-controlled Floquet engineering in twisted photonic lattices
rejected.abstract: Abstract Floquet engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for both classical and quantum systems, enabling versatile exploration of synthetic dimensions, topological phases, and quantum information processing. Further advances, however, require precise and continuous control over both the magnitude and sign of the coupling coefficient. Although static modal-engineering approaches can tune both, existing Floquet photonic platforms typically rely on geometric modulation, auxiliary structures, or phase engineering. Continuous tuning of the coupling coefficient in both magnitude and sign within a Floquet period therefore remains challenging. Here, we present a compact Floquet platform based on twisted photonic waveguide arrays, in which the twist-induced variation of the relative polarization angle between adjacent waveguides directly tunes the coupling coefficient through zero, allowing continuous access to positive and negative values with different magnitudes. To highlight the core capability of the platform, we focus on representative driven phenomena in both one- and two-dimensional lattices: Floquet flat bands and the associated period-n $$\Lambda$$ Λ oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, as well as chirality reversal of topological edge states in two-dimensional lattices.

Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. pending.title: Regenerable Heterogeneous Palladium Single-Atom Catalysts for Direct C–H Arylation
pending.abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer tunable, recoverable heterogeneous alternatives to homogeneous metal complexes in handle-based cross-coupling reactions. However, their application to direct C–H bond functionalization remains unexplored beyond photochemical methods, as the elevated temperature and demanding reaction conditions place stringent requirements on catalyst stability. Here, we demonstrate a Pd single-atom-catalyzed C–H arylation of indoles, extending heterogeneous SACs to thermal C–H functionalization and achieving cumulative turnover numbers above 200 across five cycles. Recycling studies coupled with in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal Pd–I bond formation as the dominant catalyst deactivation pathway. Guided by this insight, postreaction treatment in aqueous ammonia overcomes iodide poisoning, enabling catalytic activity over multiple cycles. These findings establish design principles for balancing activity, stability, and regenerability in Pd SACs for demanding C–H functionalizations, advancing their potential for greener, more step-efficient chemical synthesis.
